- Transition metals in the first row (3d series) typically have configurations with electrons in both 4s and 3d orbitals
- Main group elements (like Na, F, Cl) typically don't have d electrons in their valence shell

A. Cl (Chlorine): Group 17, configuration [Ne]3s²3p⁵ - No d electrons in valence
B. Cr (Chromium): Transition metal, configuration [Ar]3d⁵4s¹ - Has both s and d electrons in valence
C. F (Fluorine): Group 17, configuration [He]2s²2p⁵ - No d electrons in valence
D. Mn (Manganese): Transition metal, configuration [Ar]3d⁵4s² - Has both s and d electrons in valence
E. Na (Sodium): Group 1, configuration [Ne]3s¹ - No d electrons in valence
F. Ni (Nickel): Transition metal, configuration [Ar]3d⁸4s² - Has both s and d electrons in valence

Therefore, the elements with valence electrons in both s and d-sublevels are Cr (B), Mn (D), and Ni (F).
